propositions: A 0-byte drain lock with no owner stamp persists forever when the drainer process dies between creation and release, permanently wedging enrichment with no visible error signal
The drain lock lacks ownership metadata and staleness adjudication, causing FileExistsError on every later drain attempt without reclaim or retry
The INFO-level skip log obscures the wedge condition; real holders need to be decoded and logged at WARNING with age
A new v2 owner stamp written after O_EXCL creation enables staleness determination via shared wall-clock ceiling bound (1h) for unrecognized/torn stamps
Bounded single-retry reclaim on stale detection allows dead holders to be replaced while respecting live holders and avoiding duplicate-work races
Doctor's drain lock assessment moves from not-assessable to real staleness verdict by decoding the stamp and delegating to the shared staleness core
